With the increasing availability of granular data on the relationships between individual entities - such as persons, countries and financial institutions - network analysis offers many possibilities to extract useful information from such data. This post provides an introduction to network analysis in R using the `igraph` package.

## The `igraph` package

There are some R packages with allow to analyse networks. In this post I concentrate on the `igraph` packages, which allows for a broad range of applications.

### DebtRank

### DebtRank


```{r, message = FALSE}
library(NetworkRiskMeasures)

# Loads simulated banking data
data("sim_data")
head(sim_data)
```

```{r}
# seed for reproducibility
set.seed(15)

# minimum density estimation
# verbose = F to prevent printing
md_mat <- matrix_estimation(sim_data$assets, sim_data$liabilities, method = "md", verbose = FALSE)

# rownames and colnames for the matrix
rownames(md_mat) <- colnames(md_mat) <- sim_data$bank
```

```{r}
# DebtRank simulation
contdr <- contagion(exposures = md_mat, buffer = sim_data$buffer, weights = sim_data$weights, 
                    shock = "all", method = "debtrank", verbose = FALSE)

summary(contdr)
```

```{r, fig.height=3.5, fig.width=5}
plot(contdr)
```
